item.title: DNS Server adds Event 506 and relocates debug logs outside its default directory — 14 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 14 November 2026

DNS Server adds Event 506 and relocates debug logs outside its default directory

The period’s most consequential guidance concerns DNS logging and Windows Admin Center compatibility. Applicable 2026 cumulative updates are documented as logging DNS Event ID 506 and relocating existing debug logs configured outside `C:\Windows\System32\dns\log`; changing `LogFilePath` now requires local Administrators membership. Windows Admin Center 1.3.0.0 is documented as moving to .NET 10, with Azure Connected Machine Agent 1.65 or earlier unable to upgrade to that version or later. Failover Cluster Manager guidance also tightens the campus-cluster procedure around KB5072033, the fault-domain property, and storage-pool version.

DNS and DHCP · PowerShell and automation

DNS guidance documents new logging and permission behavior

Starting with applicable 2026 cumulative updates, DNS Server logs Event ID 506 and relocates existing debug logs configured outside `C:\Windows\System32\dns\log`. Changing `LogFilePath` requires membership in local Administrators; DnsAdmins membership alone is denied.

Management · Releases, upgrades and migration

Windows Admin Center 1.3.0.0 moves to .NET 10

The 1.3.0.0 release upgrades Windows Admin Center to .NET 10. Azure Connected Machine Agent version 1.65 or earlier cannot upgrade to this Windows Admin Center version or later versions.

Management · General

Arc agent guidance preserves connection and upgrade boundaries

The Arc hybrid-machine guidance states that agent versions 1.65 or earlier cannot upgrade to Windows Admin Center 1.0.0.0 or later. It also records that Arc agent versions 1.35 and 1.36 break Windows Admin Center connections, while version 1.37 and later fix that issue.

Failover Clustering · General

Campus-cluster instructions revise the fault-domain and storage prerequisites

The Failover Cluster Manager procedure now scopes KB5072033 to every server joining the cluster, replaces `FaultDomainAwareness` checks with `FaultDomainAwarenessDefault`, and clarifies the requirement for storage pool version 29 or later.

View all updates for 14 November 2026 →

item.title: RD Web Access XSLT customizations face Chromium M158 cutoff November 17, 2026 — 13 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 13 November 2026

RD Web Access XSLT customizations face Chromium M158 cutoff November 17, 2026

New Remote Desktop guidance covers assessing, migrating, validating, and troubleshooting RD Web Access customizations that rely on browser-native XSLT. Chromium M158 disables browser-native XSLT beginning November 17, 2026.

Remote Desktop · Releases, upgrades and migration

Migration path added for RD Web Access XSLT customizations

The guidance explains how to assess, migrate, validate, and troubleshoot customizations using browser-native XSLT. It directs administrators to keep the updated .aspx pages unchanged and configure a separate stylesheet through RDWebSiteXsltPath before Chromium M158 disables browser-native XSLT on November 17, 2026.

item.title: AD FS FAQ ties unknown domain identifiers to controller discovery and CLDAP safeguards — 12 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 12 November 2026

AD FS FAQ ties unknown domain identifiers to controller discovery and CLDAP safeguards

An updated AD FS troubleshooting FAQ explains that unrecognized domain identifiers in username and password requests can trigger domain controller discovery, including DNS SRV queries and CLDAP pings. It recommends Extranet Smart Lockout on Windows Server 2019 and later, along with restricting outbound CLDAP traffic.

AD FS · Troubleshooting

AD FS guidance details domain-controller discovery triggered by unknown identifiers

The FAQ says unrecognized domain identifiers in username and password requests can initiate domain controller discovery through DNS SRV queries and CLDAP pings. It recommends Extranet Smart Lockout for Windows Server 2019 and later and restricting outbound CLDAP traffic.

item.title: SID-bearing certificate requests: NDES guidance explains SAN, extension, and custom policy-module exception — 11 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 11 November 2026

SID-bearing certificate requests: NDES guidance explains SAN, extension, and custom policy-module exception

The 11 November batch was largely documentation maintenance, with the most substantive update in AD CS. NDES guidance now covers certificate requests carrying SID information in the SAN or a separate SID extension, including the custom policy module exception. Other meaningful edits refresh VM conversion links for VDDK 8.0.3 and Changed Block Tracking troubleshooting, while Active Directory and AD FS received narrower reference and wording updates.

AD CS · General

NDES guidance details SID data in SANs and separate certificate extensions

The AD CS article now describes NDES behavior for requests containing SID information in the SAN or in a separate SID extension, including the exception for custom policy modules. Administrators working on affected enrollment scenarios should consult this guidance during design or troubleshooting.

Management · Releases, upgrades and migration

VM conversion guidance links directly to Broadcom for VDDK 8.0.3

The migration procedure now points to Broadcom Support for downloading VMware VDDK 8.0.3. The required version and extraction path remain unchanged, so the practical action is to use the updated download link.

Management · Troubleshooting

Changed Block Tracking troubleshooting now uses a new Broadcom guide URL

The VM conversion troubleshooting article now links to a new Broadcom VDDK Programming Guide URL for Changed Block Tracking troubleshooting. Administrators following the article will be directed to that updated resource.

Active Directory · General

Active Directory security guidance now links to OWASP’s 2025 Top 10

The Avenues To Compromise article replaces its former OWASP index link with the OWASP 2025 Top 10 page, directing readers to current vulnerability and countermeasure information. No configuration change is required.

AD FS · General

AD FS smart-lockout guidance revises proxy request wording and metadata

The AD FS extranet smart lockout article received updated DevRel metadata links and a minor revision describing ESL requests through Web Application Proxy or an MS-ADFSPIP-compatible third-party proxy. No administrator action is indicated.

View all updates for 11 November 2026 →

item.title: NDES guidance adds SID certificate request settings and validation safeguards — 7 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 7 November 2026

NDES guidance adds SID certificate request settings and validation safeguards

A new AD CS article explains how to configure NDES to accept SID information in certificate requests through registry settings for SAN URI and NTDS CA security extension formats.

AD CS · General

New AD CS guidance covers SID-enabled NDES requests

The article documents registry configuration for accepting SID information in certificate requests, including SAN URI and NTDS CA security extension formats. It advises that a trusted component validate the SID before enabling these settings and specifies resetting IIS or restarting NDES to apply changes.

View all updates for 7 November 2026 →
